Jerioth
jēr′ī-ōth
n. (a wife of Caleb the son of Hezron, of the tribe of Judah)
Hebrew Yerioth (H3408), curtains, tent-curtains, plural of yeri'ah, a curtain such as those of the tabernacle.

Biblical Definition

Jerioth appears once, in the genealogy of Judah kept by the Chronicler: “And Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth: her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon” (1 Chronicles 2:18). She is named alongside Azubah as a wife (or, by some readings of the Hebrew, possibly as a further description of Azubah herself) of this Caleb son of Hezron, a Judahite genealogically distinct from the more famous Caleb the son of Jephunneh who spied out the land. Her name, meaning curtains, is the very word used throughout Exodus for the ten linen curtains of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:1), a striking word to carry as a personal name in a family that stood, generation by generation, in the tribal line from which the tabernacle’s own priesthood-adjacent leadership and later David’s throne would come. This Caleb’s house continues immediately in the record: after Azubah’s death he took Ephrath, who bare him Hur (1 Chronicles 2:19), the ancestor, several generations on, of Bethlehem (1 Chronicles 2:50–51) and so of the messianic line. Jerioth’s sons stand at the root of that same reckoned house.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Jerioth; her name means curtains, the same word used of the tabernacle hangings, and she is a wife of Caleb the son of Hezron in the Chronicler's genealogy of Judah.

expand to see more

JERIOTH, n. A wife of Caleb the son of Hezron, of the tribe of Judah, named in the Chronicler's genealogy.

CURTAIN, n. A hanging cloth, used in Scripture especially of the linen and goats'-hair hangings of the tabernacle.

GENEALOGY, n. An account or history of the descent of persons or families from an ancestor.

TRIBE, n. A family, race, or series of generations descended from the same progenitor.

HEZRON, n. A son of Pharez, grandson of Judah, from whom descended the family of Caleb and, eventually, David.

Key Scripture

1 Chronicles 2:18 — "And Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth: her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon."

1 Chronicles 2:19 — "And when Azubah was dead, Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur."

1 Chronicles 2:9 — "The sons also of Hezron, that were born unto him; Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai."

1 Chronicles 2:50 — "These were the sons of Caleb the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephratah; Shobal the father of Kirjathjearim."

Modern Corruption

A single-verse woman in a dense tribal genealogy, preserved without embellishment or legend, argues for a genuine archival source behind Chronicles, not late nationalist invention.

expand to see more

A minimalist historiography that treats the Chronicler’s genealogies as post-exilic legitimating fiction, composed to give the returned community a usable past, has to account for names like Jerioth — too minor, too textually difficult, and too narratively unrewarding to have been invented for propaganda. A forger inventing an ancestry does not bother with a nearly-anonymous second wife whose sons do nothing notable; a compiler working from real family records does.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD’s providence in the small links of a long chain: an obscure wife of an obscure Caleb, in an obscure verse, sits within the very tribal house from which Hur, Bethlehem, and ultimately David and Christ descend (1 Chronicles 2:50–51) — every generation matters to the God who counts them all.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yeri'ah (H3407), curtain; Chetsron (H2696), Hezron; Kalev (H3612), Caleb; toledoth (H8435), generations.

expand to see more

Hebrew yeri'ah (H3407) — curtain; the singular of the plural yerioth behind her name.

Hebrew Chetsron (H2696) — Hezron, the father of Caleb and grandfather of Jerioth’s sons.

Hebrew Kalev (H3612) — Caleb, Jerioth’s husband, wholehearted or dog-like in devotion.

Hebrew toledoth (H8435) — generations; the Chronicler’s governing structure.

Hebrew ben (H1121) — son; the word introducing each name in the register.

Usage

"“Caleb the son of Hezron begat children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth” — her single appearance in the text."

"“Her sons are these; Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon” — the line she leaves behind."

"“Caleb took unto him Ephrath, which bare him Hur” — the house continuing toward Bethlehem."
